that killed hundreds would not pose a material risk to its financial results.

Chief Executive Ricardo Jaramillo told Reuters the company now expects net profit between 2.5 trillion pesos ($805.09 million) and 2.7 trillion pesos ($869.50 million), up from a previous range of 2.3 trillion to 2.5 trillion pesos.
He said Grupo SURA expects net profit to reach around 3 trillion pesos ($959.7 million) in 2027 and 3.3 trillion pesos ($1.06 billion) in 2028.
The group reported first-half net profit of 1.68 trillion pesos, up 38% from the same period a year earlier.
The improved outlook reflects stronger performance across Grupo SURA's insurance, asset management and banking businesses.

Jaramillo said August's earthquake could result in a temporary effect on working capital as claims are paid before reimbursements arrive from international reinsurers. The event will not threaten its year-end targets, he said.
Jaramillo said the company plans to repay 1.5 trillion pesos of debt this year using dividends and cash from operations, cutting debt by about 20% in the second half and easing interest costs.
That would help support shareholder returns, including dividend growth and a proposed share buyback.
Grupo SURA will ask shareholders this week to approve a repurchase program of up to 500 billion pesos. If approved, buybacks would begin near the end of the year.
